title: 130 Journal Prompts for Every Day (Free List)
description: 130 journal prompts sorted by theme: everyday life, memories, feelings, relationships, goals and fun. Pick one and write your answer right on this page.
h1: 130 journal prompts to help you start writing
intro: Journal prompts are short questions that give you something to write about when the page feels blank. Below are **130 journal prompts** grouped by theme, from easy everyday questions to deeper ones about who you are. Pick one, press Write, and answer it in the diary at the top of this page.

writer.title: Today's prompt
writer.hint: Pick a prompt below and press Write, or just start here

sections.h2: How to use these journaling prompts

blocks.p: You do not need to answer every question, and you do not need to go in order. Read down the list until one makes you pause. That pause is a good sign. It means you have something to say.

steps.name: Pick one prompt.
steps.text: One is enough. If a question feels too big today, choose a lighter one from the everyday list.

steps.name: Press Write.
steps.text: The prompt loads into the diary at the top of the page. Your words stay saved in this browser on this device.

steps.name: Write for five minutes.
steps.text: Do not fix spelling or worry about sounding smart. Keep your pen, or your fingers, moving.

steps.name: End with one line.
steps.text: Finish with one thing you noticed or want to remember. That line is often the most useful part.

blocks.tip: New to this? Read our guide on [how to start a journal](/how-to-start-a-journal/) or try the gentle list of [journaling prompts for beginners](/journaling-prompts-for-beginners/).

blocks.p: These are quick and easy. They work well on busy days or when you want to keep a [daily journal](/daily-journal/) habit going.

prompts: What was the best ten minutes of your day, and what made it good?
Write down three things you heard today: a sound, a sentence and a song.
What did you eat today that you would happily eat again tomorrow?
Describe the view from the window closest to you right now.
What took longer than you expected today, and why?
Who did you talk to the most today? What did you talk about?
What is one small thing you finished today, even if nobody noticed?
Describe your mood right now as if it were the weather.
What is sitting on your to-do list that you keep moving to tomorrow?
What made you smile today without trying?
If today had a title like a book chapter, what would it be?
What did you learn today, big or tiny?
Describe the outfit you wore today and how it made you feel.
What is one thing you would do differently if you could replay today?
What are you looking forward to this week?
Describe the house you lived in when you were seven. Walk through it room by room.
What was your favorite toy as a child, and where is it now?
Write about a teacher who changed how you saw yourself.
What smell takes you straight back to childhood?
Describe the first time you felt truly grown up.
What is the best meal you have ever eaten? Who were you with?
Write about a trip that did not go as planned but turned out fine.
What song was playing everywhere the summer you were sixteen?
Describe a family tradition you loved, or one you were glad to leave behind.
Write about a time you got lost, in a city or in life.
What is a memory you replay when you need cheering up?
Describe your first job and the people you worked with.
What is something you believed as a kid that makes you laugh now?
Write about a friendship from school. What happened to it?

sections.h2: Journal prompts to get to know yourself

blocks.p: These questions help you notice what you value and how you think. For a longer list, see our [journal prompts for self-discovery](/journal-prompts-for-self-discovery/) and [values journal prompts](/journal-prompts-values/).

prompts: What three words would your closest friend use to describe you? Do you agree?
What do you do when you have a free afternoon and no plans?
What topic could you talk about for an hour without notes?
When do you feel most like yourself?
What is a rule you live by that nobody taught you?
What is something you changed your mind about in the last year?
Which compliment do you remember years later? Why did it stick?
What drains your energy faster than anything else?
What do you secretly hope people notice about you?
Describe your perfect ordinary Tuesday, from waking up to bedtime.
What are you proud of that you rarely mention?
What would your twelve-year-old self think of your life today?
Which habit of yours would you most like to keep forever?
What do you pretend to like that you actually do not?

sections.h2: Journal prompts for feelings and mental health

blocks.p: Writing about feelings can make them easier to name and carry. If you want more support, try our lists of [journal prompts for mental health](/journal-prompts-for-mental-health/), [journal prompts for anxiety](/journal-prompts-for-anxiety/) and [healing journal prompts](/healing-journal-prompts/).

prompts: What feeling has shown up the most this week? When does it usually arrive?
Where in your body do you feel stress first? What helps it loosen?
Write about something that is bothering you, then write what you would tell a friend in the same spot.
What do you need more of right now: rest, company, quiet or fun?
What is a worry you can do something about this week? What is one you cannot?
Describe a time you handled a hard moment better than you expected.
What thought keeps looping in your head lately? Write it out in full.
Which people leave you feeling calmer after you see them?
What is something you have been carrying that you could put down?
Finish this sentence five times: Right now I feel...
What does a good day for your mind look like?
When was the last time you cried? What was underneath it?
What is one kind thing you can do for yourself tonight?
List what is in your control today and what is not.

blocks.p: For more on friends, family and love, see our full list of [journal prompts on relationships](/journal-prompts-on-relationships/).

prompts: Who do you call when something good happens? Why them?
Write about a friend you have lost touch with. What would you say if you met today?
What did your family teach you about money, love or work without ever saying it?
Describe the moment you knew someone had become a real friend.
What is a conversation you keep putting off? What is the first sentence?
Who has shown up for you when it counted?
What do you need from people that you find hard to ask for?
Write a thank you note to someone who will never read it.
What kind of friend are you on your best day?
Which relationship in your life feels easiest right now? Which feels hardest?
Describe someone you admire who you also know well.
What is a boundary you set that you are glad you kept?
What would you like the people you love to know about you?

sections.h2: Journal prompts for goals and the future

blocks.p: Use these when you want to plan, dream or check in on where you are heading. For yearly goals, try our [new year journal prompts](/journal-prompts-new-year/). For bigger personal change, see [journal prompts for self-growth](/journal-prompts-for-self-growth/).

prompts: Write a letter to yourself to open one year from today.
What would you try if you knew nobody would laugh at you?
What is one skill you would like to be good at in five years?
Describe where you want to be living ten years from now, down to the kitchen.
What goal did you give up on? Do you still want it?
What is the smallest step you could take toward a big dream this week?
What does success mean to you, in your own words?
Which part of your life needs the most attention this month?
What are you saying yes to that you would like to say no to?
Write about a fear that keeps you from starting something.
Who is already living a life you want? What do they do daily?
What would make next year better than this one?
If you had one extra hour every day, how would you use it?
What do you want to be remembered for?

blocks.p: These lift your mood fast. For a full list, see our [gratitude journal prompts](/gratitude-journal-prompts/) and the guide to keeping a [gratitude journal](/gratitude-journal/).

prompts: What is a simple pleasure you would miss if it disappeared tomorrow?
Which object in your home makes you happy every time you see it?
Describe a stranger who was kind to you.
What is something about your body you are thankful for today?
What are you glad you did not get, looking back?
Describe your favorite place to sit outdoors.
What made you laugh out loud recently?
Which season do you love most, and what do you love about it?
What is a skill you have that makes life easier?
Write about a hard time that taught you something you are glad to know.
What small luxury makes an ordinary day feel special?
Who made your life easier this month without being asked?

blocks.p: Not every entry has to be serious. These are playful and good for warming up. For more, browse our [journal ideas](/journal-ideas/).

prompts: You can have dinner with any person who ever lived. Who is it, and what do you order?
Describe your dream home in a place you have never been.
Write a short review of your week as if it were a restaurant.
If your life had a theme song, what would it be?
Invent a holiday. What is it called, and how do people celebrate?
Write a scene where you meet yourself at age eighty.
What would you do with a free plane ticket to anywhere, leaving tomorrow?
Describe a perfect rainy day from start to finish.
If you opened a small shop, what would you sell?
Make a list of ten things that are blue and mean something to you.
Write about your day from your pet's point of view, or a houseplant's.
What would you name a boat, and why?
If you could master any instrument overnight, which would you pick?
Write the first page of your autobiography.

sections.h2: Reflective journal prompts for the end of the week

blocks.p: Looking back helps you notice patterns. For more, see our [reflective journal prompts](/reflective-journal-prompts/) or use [journal prompts before bed](/journal-prompts-before-bed/) to close out each day.

prompts: What went better this week than last week?
What drained you this week, and can you avoid it next week?
Who did you help this week? Who helped you?
What is one thing you want to remember from these seven days?
Did you keep the promises you made to yourself? Which ones slipped?
What is one habit you want to carry into next week?
Rate your week from one to ten. What would have made it one point higher?
What surprised you about yourself this week?
What did you spend money on that was worth it?
What news, idea or conversation stuck with you?
Where did you waste time, and did you enjoy it anyway?
What are three words that sum up this week?
What did you put off that you can finish in under an hour?
What are you letting go of before the new week starts?
Write one sentence of encouragement for yourself next Monday.
What question do you want to sit with next week?
What did this week teach you about what you need?
Name one thing you did this week that took courage, however small.
What do you want next week to feel like?
Which day this week felt the longest, and which one flew by?

sections.h2: Tips for using a journal prompts list

ul: **Same time, same place.** Writing after your morning coffee or right before bed turns prompts into a habit you do not have to think about.
**Go sideways.** If a prompt leads you somewhere else, follow it. The prompt is a door, not a rule.
**Answer the same prompt twice.** Pick a question you answered months ago and answer it again. Comparing the two is eye opening.
**Keep it short on hard days.** One honest sentence counts as journaling.
**Make it printable.** Use your browser's Print or Save as PDF to keep a paper copy of your answers, or grab our [printable journal pages](/printable-journal-pages/).
**Keep it private.** Your entries here are saved only in this browser on this device. No account, no sign up.

blocks.tip: Stuck even with a prompt? Write: I do not know what to write because... and keep going. It works more often than you would think.

faq.a: A journal prompt is a question or short idea that gives you something to write about. It removes the hardest part of journaling, which is staring at a blank page. A good prompt is specific, like asking about the best ten minutes of your day, so you can start writing right away instead of wondering where to begin.

faq.q: What should I write in my journal every day?
faq.a: Start with three short parts: what happened today, how you felt about it, and one thing you want to remember or do tomorrow. On days you want more, pick a prompt from the list above. Even five minutes a day is enough to build the habit. Our guide on [what to write in a journal](/what-to-write-in-a-journal/) has more ideas.

faq.q: How many journal prompts should I answer at once?
faq.a: One is usually best. A single prompt answered honestly gives you more than five answered in a rush. If you have extra time, answer one light prompt to warm up and one deeper prompt after that. Save the rest of the list for other days so it stays fresh.

faq.q: Are journal prompts good for mental health?
faq.a: Many people find that writing about their thoughts and feelings helps them feel calmer and see problems more clearly. Research on expressive writing has found it can help some people process stress. Journaling is a helpful habit, but it is not a replacement for care from a doctor or counselor when you need it.

faq.q: Can I print these journal prompts or get them as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Use your browser's Print option and choose Save as PDF to keep the full list. Anything you write in the diary on this page can be printed the same way. You can also use our [journal template](/journal-template/) if you prefer to fill in a page on paper.

faq.q: What if a prompt brings up hard feelings?
faq.a: That is normal. You can stop at any time, switch to a lighter prompt, or close the page. Writing a few lines about what came up and one kind thing you can do next often helps. If you feel unsafe or in crisis, contact local emergency services. In the US, you can call or text 988.
